pairs.difference: B (UFO): the five-level lens shows a pale ring-shaped glow around the saucer, with the corners stepping down to darker green. That spotlight-halo grouping matches the generated lesson cards. The dome is the darkest accent, and the hull's lit band clips to white with hard edges. A (umbrella): the background rings stay at an even mid value, and the canopy splits into clear light-yellow and dark-red underside groups. There is no halo behind it.
pairs.fix: Keep the green background one even mid-tone across the whole card, with no bright glow behind the saucer. Shade the metal hull softly from light on top to mid-grey below, without bright white streaks.

pairs.difference: B (airplane): the whole lower half and the edges are near-white cloud, and the white fuselage sits on white cloud. The hero hardly separates from the background by value, and the edges are brighter than the centre (vignette -0.056). A (rocket): the mid-grey sky makes a clean middle group, the rocket body is mid-to-light against it, and the clouds form a separate light band at the bottom.
pairs.fix: Put the plane against a clear mid-blue patch of sky, keep the clouds below and behind it smaller, and let the card's corners stay slightly darker than the centre.

pairs.difference: B (yellow UFO): the hull reads as one light-to-mid mass, and the only darks are thin black rims on the engine pods. The edges are brighter than the centre because of the white clouds (vignette -0.072). A (balloons): it has large dark groups in the purple and red balloons and a mid-teal middle, set against mid sky with light clouds below. The light, middle and dark masses are clear.
pairs.fix: Give the saucer a clearly darker shaded underside. Keep the clouds low and small so the corners don't turn white, and add one or two mid-dark shapes to the hull.

pairs.difference: B (star chart): about half the card is a solid near-black navy panel in the centre, with tiny white stars. The darkest accent covers a huge area, and the overall key drops to 0.57. A (map): the hero is mostly light, the table is mid, and the only dark accent is the small black lens handle, which matches how real cards place their darkest spots.
pairs.fix: Make the chart's background a medium blue instead of near-black, and keep the deepest darks to small spots such as the frame shadow.

pairs.difference: A (ice tray): a bright white glow bursts out behind the ice cube, a spotlight halo like the one in the generated lessons. The background corners step down to darker grey, and frosty white speckles create hard little contrasts on the tray. B (pool): the darkest areas are the dark fence top-left and the dark grass edges, and the light spot sits on the water. It has no halo, though the textures are noisy.
pairs.fix: Remove the white glow behind the ice cube and keep the sky-ray background an even mid-blue. Use fewer frost speckles so the pink tray reads as smooth mid-tones.

pairs.difference: A (battery): the floor clips to a large near-white area, and the glass cylinder is mostly light and see-through, so the hero merges with the light floor. Only the metal caps give mid-dark accents. B (vending machine): the dark-blue body is a strong dark mass against a mid-purple background, and the light window inside gives clear groups.
pairs.fix: Make the pink floor a soft mid-tone with no bright white patch. Give the battery's glass a darker tint and its metal caps deeper shading so it stands out from the floor.

pairs.difference: A (sandcastle): the card is almost all light. Sand and castle are the same pale value, rms contrast is 0.118 (below the real range) and the mean is 0.771 (above it). The castle separates from the sand only by hue. B (bumper car): it has a dark base and steering wheel, a mid-green body and a light-orange background, so the light, middle and dark groups are clear.
pairs.fix: Shade the castle's shadow sides clearly darker than the sunlit sand, deepen the shadows in the doorways, windows and under the bucket, and make the sand in the foreground slightly darker.

pairs.difference: A (drone): a huge pure-white starburst glow fills the centre behind the drone, so the mean is 0.831, far above the real range. The pale white body disappears into the glow, and only the black rotor discs carry the contrast. B (street lamp): a mid-tone teal background with even rays, and a dark lamp silhouette against it with its light kept to the glass.
pairs.fix: Remove the bright white glow behind the drone. Keep the yellow ray background one even mid-tone, and give the drone body grey shaded sides so it doesn't merge with the background.

pairs.difference: B (antenna): a thin white pole on a pale grey rooftop with near-white sky clouds. Contrast is very low (rms 0.068), the mean is 0.777, and the only dark is the cast shadow. A (lighthouse): it matches the real lesson card, with a dark-red band and gallery against mid sky and light clouds.
pairs.fix: Make the antenna mast mid-grey with darker metal clamps, draw the rooftop a darker grey, and use a deeper blue sky so the mast stands out by brightness.

pairs.difference: B (bike on car): the top of the card is a near-white sky band while the bottom holds near-black tyres and a black rack. The edges are far brighter than the centre (vignette -0.318), and contrast is very hard (rms 0.232). Both are outside the real range. A (rover): dark purple sky at the top, light rover in the middle, mid-grey ground. The grouping is clear, if a little dark at the corners.
pairs.fix: Use a mid-tone sky instead of a bright white-gold one, lighten the black tyres and rack to dark grey, and frame the bike as a single centred object.

pairs.difference: B (tablet): a heavy black bezel frames a single flat mid-value screen, and a white brushed-metal streak runs along the left edge. The edges are brighter than the centre (vignette -0.052), and contrast is a bit harsh (rms 0.2). A (book): mid-teal cover on a mid-to-light wooden table, with light page edges and small light stickers. The groups are gentle.
pairs.fix: Draw the tablet bezel dark grey rather than black, add soft shading across the screen, and make the metal background an even mid-grey without bright streaks at the edges.

pairs.difference: B (helmet): the background is lightest right behind the helmet and darkens to the corners, a spotlight halo. The white shell clips to hard white next to a very dark visor reflection, so contrast inside the hero is hard. A (sneakers): a flat two-tone wall and floor with no halo. The dark-blue shoe bodies stand against a light floor, with soft shading.
pairs.fix: Keep the purple background one even tone with no light patch behind the helmet. Shade the white shell softly into light grey, and keep the visor a mid-dark gold instead of black.

pattern: On value alone, generated cards give themselves away in four ways. First, a spotlight glow sits right behind the hero, so the background is lightest in the middle and darkens toward the corners (UFO, ice tray, drone, helmet). Second, large areas go near-white, such as floors, skies and cloud banks, which pushes the card's brightness outside the real range or makes the edges brighter than the centre. Third, the darkest tones either cover a big area (the black star chart, the black tablet bezel) or barely appear at all, so the hero stands out by hue but not by brightness. Fourth, contrast inside the hero is hard, with white highlights right next to near-black, where real cards shade gradually.
